answer:
Here is what I would raise at your check-up, most important first. The records I have run to 15 October 2026, so anything done at another clinic or after that date will not show here. Please check these points with your doctor.

1. Your stool test (FIT) from 4 November 2025 came back positive. I cannot find a colonoscopy or any other bowel follow-up after it. A positive result normally leads to a colonoscopy, so this is the most urgent item. If that has not happened, call the office before your appointment.

2. Metformin was stopped on 15 April 2024, and the records give no reason. Your next diabetes medicine, empagliflozin (Jardiance), was not started until 20 February 2025. Over that gap your A1c (a blood sugar average over about three months) rose from 6.7% to 8.3%. Ask why metformin was stopped and whether you went without diabetes treatment.

3. Your last A1c was 6.9% on 16 February 2026. That is more than eight months ago. With diabetes it is usually checked at least every six months, so it is due.

4. Cholesterol: in February 2025 your LDL was 131 and your total cholesterol was 212, both high. You started atorvastatin on 20 February 2025. No cholesterol test has been recorded since, so a recheck is probably due.

5. Kidneys: your eGFR (a kidney filtering number) was 69 in February 2026, down from 73 a year earlier. That is still above the usual cut-off of 60. No urine albumin test appears anywhere in the records. People with diabetes normally have one every year.

6. Blood count: none appears in the records. Since your stool test was positive, ask whether a blood count should be checked for anemia, which can come from slow bleeding.

7. Blood pressure: no reading appears anywhere in these records. Ask for one at the check-up.

8. Your condition list still includes pulmonary embolism (a clot in the lung). The CT scan in July 2025 found no clot, and the entry is marked as refuted. Ask your doctor to confirm it is not a current diagnosis and to correct the list.

9. Diabetes checks: I see no eye exam (retinal or dilated) and no foot exam recorded. Both are usually done every year for diabetes.

The records may be incomplete, for example if other clinics ran tests, so treat this as a list of questions for your doctor rather than a diagnosis.
short: Positive stool test (Nov 2025) with no colonoscopy recorded. Last A1c was 6.9% in Feb 2026. No cholesterol, urine albumin, blood count, blood pressure, eye or foot checks are recorded. Metformin stopped Apr 2024 with no reason given. A pulmonary embolism entry is marked refuted.
